name: SYRIA

flag.title: Flag of Syria
flag.note: Green, white & black with 2 red stars

lead: Syria sits where three continents meet. The first farmers planted seeds here 12,000 years ago. People have lived in its capital, Damascus, since before the pyramids.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Syria has three faces. A thin green strip of coast grows citrus fruit. Mountains rise behind it. Then steppe (dry grassland) and desert cover more than half the country.
The Euphrates River crosses the northeast and waters fields of wheat and cotton. Near Hama, wooden water wheels have scooped up river water for over 600 years.
animals: Syria lies on a busy bird highway. Each spring and autumn, millions of storks, eagles and songbirds fly through.
The reem gazelle sprints across the steppe. It is on Syria's new banknotes. Striped hyenas hunt at night. Wolves roam the mountains.
culture: Syrian food is about 10,000 years old. Many world favourites were perfected here, like flatbread from clay ovens, hummus and slow-cooked lamb.
The Damask rose is named after Damascus. It blooms every May outside the capital. Farmers pick the petals at dawn and make rose water, which perfumers worldwide still use.
history: People lived near Damascus as far back as 10,000 BC. By 3000 BC, the city of Ebla had a royal library of 17,000 clay tablets. Most of Europe still lived in wooden huts.
Syria later sat on the Silk Road, which linked China to the Mediterranean. Merchants swapped silk, spices, glass and stories in Aleppo's covered market for centuries.
wows: Every pet hamster alive today comes from one family found near Aleppo in 1930.
Damascus has been lived in non-stop for at least 10,000 years, one of Earth's oldest cities.
Syria has six UNESCO World Heritage Sites (protected places), among the most in the Middle East.
A few mountain villages still speak Aramaic, the language Jesus likely spoke.
Aleppo's Al-Madina Souk is 13 km long, one of the longest covered markets.
Hama's wooden water wheels, up to 21 m tall, were the world's tallest for nearly 500 years.
Syria's 2026 banknotes show the Damask rose, a swallow and a gazelle, not politicians.

myths.myth: The Silk Road was one long road
myths.fact: It was a web of many routes over land and sea. Goods passed from hand to hand.

myths.myth: Arabic numerals were invented in Arabia
myths.fact: They began in India. Arab scholars spread them west, so Europeans called them Arabic.
